moduleTitle: Module 1. Foundations, Membranes and Cell Signaling

competencies.name: Signal types and range
competencies.can: Classify a chemical signal as autocrine, paracrine, neurotransmitter, neurohormone, or hormone by its route and distance of travel.

competencies.name: Receptor location and ligand solubility
competencies.can: Predict whether a signal molecule binds a surface receptor or an intracellular receptor from its lipid solubility and relate that to the speed and duration of the response.

competencies.name: G protein coupled receptors
competencies.can: Trace a G protein coupled receptor pathway from ligand binding through the G protein and amplifier enzyme to the second messenger and the cellular response.

competencies.name: Second messengers
competencies.can: Identify cyclic AMP, IP3, diacylglycerol, and calcium as second messengers and state the enzyme that generates each and one target it activates.

competencies.name: Catalytic receptors and intracellular receptors
competencies.can: Compare a receptor enzyme such as the insulin receptor with an intracellular steroid receptor by mechanism and by time course of the response.

competencies.name: Signal amplification
competencies.can: Explain how a cascade amplifies a signal and estimate the size of the amplification across the steps of a given pathway.

competencies.name: Receptor modulation
competencies.can: Define agonist, antagonist, competitive inhibition, up regulation, and down regulation and predict the effect of chronic ligand excess on target cell sensitivity.

competencies.name: Signal termination
competencies.can: Name three mechanisms that end a chemical signal and explain why a signal that cannot be terminated produces pathology.

competencies.name: Dose response relationships
competencies.can: Plot a dose response curve, identify threshold, maximal response, and EC50, and compare a full agonist with a partial agonist on the same axes.
